extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / graduate students studying complex analysis, elliptic curves, and modular forms
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition proving analytic properties of the Weierstrass ℘-function (periodicity, Laurent series, derivative, differential equation, and uniformisation to an elliptic curve) and introducing level-N congruence subgroups, modular forms (weak and full), q-expansions, and Hecke operators. Suitable as a chapter/lecture in a course on elliptic functions and modular forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform convergence implies holomorphic limit and differentiated termwise
rubrics_metrics.description: Holomorphic functions that uniformly converge on compact sets converge to a holomorphic function whose derivative is the limit of the derivatives (using Cauchy's Integral Formula).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to justify termwise differentiation of the Weierstrass series: the derivative of ℘ equals the sum of the derivatives of its summands, and that resulting series converges uniformly on compact sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formula for ℘′ (derivative of Weierstrass ℘)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This series converges uniformly on compact sets (so defines a holomorphic function on C\L) and is L-periodic. It also shows ℘′ is odd.

rubrics_metrics.name: ℘ is even and L-periodic
rubrics_metrics.description: The Weierstrass ℘-function is even (℘(−z)=℘(z)) and periodic with respect to the lattice L: ℘(z+ω)=℘(z) for all ω ∈ L, z ∈ C\L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodicity can be shown directly from the definition or by integrating ℘′ along translated contours and using the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus plus connectivity of C\L.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laurent expansion of ℘ and relation to Eisenstein series
rubrics_metrics.description: ℘(z) = 1/z^2 + ∑_{n=1}^∞ (n+1)G_{n+2}(L) z^n, with odd G_k(L)=0, so ℘ is even.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived by expanding 1/(z−ω)^2 in powers of z/ω for |z| smaller than all nonzero lattice points and swapping sums; shows connection between ℘'s local expansion and Eisenstein series G_k(L).

rubrics_metrics.name: Differential equation for ℘ (elliptic curve equation)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verified by matching Laurent series non-positive exponent terms; implies (℘(z), ℘′(z)) lies on the cubic curve y^2 = 4x^3 + 60G4 x − 140G6. Further work required to show the cubic is non-singular (hence an elliptic curve).

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformisation map C/L → elliptic curve
rubrics_metrics.description: The map z + L ↦ (℘(z), ℘′(z)) (and 0 ↦ O) gives a bijection between C/L and the cubic curve y^2 = 4x^3 − 60G4(L)x − 140G6(L).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof checklist: show bijectivity (analyze zeros/poles of f(z)=℘(z)−x using argument principle and multiplicities) and that the map is a group homomorphism (use intersection properties of lines with the cubic and argument principle on logarithmic derivatives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-singularity test via half-period values
rubrics_metrics.description: The cubic 4x^3 − 60G4(L)x − 140G6(L) has three distinct roots given by ℘(ω1/2), ℘(ω2/2), ℘((ω1+ω2)/2); these are simple roots corresponding to places where ℘′ vanishes, so the curve is non-singular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show ℘′(half-period)=0 and multiplicity two zero of f at those points; use counting of zeros on a fundamental parallelogram to conclude distinctness of these x-values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Principal congruence subgroup Γ(N)
rubrics_metrics.description: Γ(N) is the subgroup of SL2(Z) consisting of matrices whose entries are congruent to the identity matrix mod N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Γ(N) is the kernel of the reduction map SL2(Z) → SL2(Z/NZ); it is a normal subgroup and SL2(Z)/Γ(N) is finite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Congruence subgroup and level
rubrics_metrics.description: A congruence subgroup is a subgroup of SL2(Z) that contains some principal congruence subgroup Γ(N). The minimal N for which Γ(N) ⊂ Γ is called the level of Γ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Γ0(N) (matrices with lower-left entry ≡ 0 mod N). Any congruence subgroup has finite index in SL2(Z).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Γ0(N)
rubrics_metrics.description: For positive integer N, Γ0(N) = { matrices in SL2(Z) whose bottom-left entry is 0 mod N }.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Γ0(N) is the preimage of the subgroup of upper-triangular matrices in SL2(Z/NZ) under the reduction map; contains Γ(N).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma: SL2(Z)/Γ finite for congruence subgroups
rubrics_metrics.description: For any congruence subgroup Γ, the quotient SL2(Z)/Γ is finite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Γ contains Γ(N) for some N and SL2(Z)/Γ(N) ≅ image of reduction map, which is finite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Weakly modular form of weight k for Γ
rubrics_metrics.description: A holomorphic function f : H → C is weakly modular of weight k for Γ if f(γ(z)) = j(γ,z)^k f(z) for all γ = (a b; c d) ∈ Γ and z ∈ H, where j(γ,z)=cz+d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Said equivalently: f is invariant of weight k under the action of Γ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic consequence of congruence subgroup membership
rubrics_metrics.description: If Γ contains the translation matrix (1 1; 0 1)^h for some smallest positive integer h, then any weakly modular form f for Γ satisfies f(z+h) = f(z).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus f can be expressed as a function g(q) with q = exp(2π i z / h) defined on the punctured unit disc; periodicity determines the q-change of variables for Fourier expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holomorphic at infinity (q-expansion criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: A weakly modular form f is 'holomorphic at infinity' if its associated g(q) (via q = e^{2π i z/h}) can be continued holomorphically to q=0, equivalently its q-expansion has no negative powers of q (no principal part).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently: f is bounded for Im(z) sufficiently large. Riemann's removable singularity theorem connects boundedness near q=0 to holomorphic extendability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Modular form of weight k for Γ
rubrics_metrics.description: f is a modular form of weight k for Γ if (1) f is weakly modular of weight k for Γ and (2) f[α]_k is holomorphic at ∞ for all α ∈ SL2(Z), where f[α]_k(z) = j(α,z)^{-k} f(α(z)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condition (2) ensures correct behavior at all cusps (not just ∞) by checking holomorphy after all SL2(Z)-translates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and property of the slash operator f[α]_k
rubrics_metrics.description: For α = (a b; c d), define f[α]_k(z) = j(α,z)^{-k} f(α(z)) with j(α,z)=cz+d. This transforms weak modularity between conjugate groups: if f is weakly modular for Γ then f[α]_k is weakly modular for α^{-1} Γ α.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemmas: j(β,γ(z)) j(γ,z) = j(βγ,z); α′(z)=1/(cz+d)^2; derivative and logarithmic-derivative transformation formulas are provided for contour integral manipulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: cusp and holomorphicness at all cusps
rubrics_metrics.description: Cusps are equivalence classes of Q∪{∞} under Γ (or SL2(Z)). Being holomorphic at all cusps means f[α]_k is holomorphic at ∞ for every α ∈ SL2(Z).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holomorphic at cusp corresponds to no negative q-powers in the q-expansion at that cusp; cuspidal forms vanish at all cusps (zero at q=0 in expansions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mn and finiteness of Γ-orbits
rubrics_metrics.description: Mn = set of 2×2 integer matrices of determinant n. The set of orbits SL2(Z)\,Mn (and hence Γ\Mn for a congruence subgroup Γ) is finite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Row operations by SL2(Z) reduce any matrix in Mn to a finite list of representatives; finite orbits underpin the finite sums in Hecke operators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orbit-invariance of the slash operator: f[µ1]_k = f[µ2]_k on same Γ-orbit
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is a modular form of weight k on Γ and µ1, µ2 ∈ Mn lie in the same orbit in Γ\Mn (i.e., µ2 = γ µ1 for some γ ∈ Γ), then f[µ1]_k = f[µ2]_k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures the Hecke operator defined by summing over orbit representatives is well-defined (independent of chosen representatives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and modularity preservation of Hecke operator Tn
rubrics_metrics.description: For positive integer n and modular forms f of weight k on Γ, choose representatives µ1,…,µℓ of Γ\Mn. Define T_n(f) = n^{k-1} ∑_{i=1}^ℓ f[µ_i]_k. The result T_n(f) is again a modular form of weight k for Γ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finiteness of orbit set makes the sum finite; invariance under Γ and holomorphy at cusps are checked by conjugating representatives and bounding q-expansions, respectively. Eigenforms are modular forms which are eigenvectors for all T_n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hecke-eigenform convention for rational elliptic curves (Taniyama–Shimura–Weil)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the modular form f associated to a rational elliptic curve, T_n(f) = λ_n f for some λ_n ∈ C; for prime p the eigenvalue λ_p equals a_p, the p-th Fourier coefficient related to the curve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ties modular forms (eigenforms) to arithmetic of elliptic curves; historically central to modularity theorem proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument-principle modifications under SL2(Z) action
rubrics_metrics.description: When transforming contours by α ∈ SL2(Z), integrals of f′/f pick up extra terms: ∮_{α(γ)} f′/f = ∮_γ (f[α]_k)′/f[α]_k + k ∮_γ j′(α)/j(α,z) dz.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to count zeros/poles of modular/cusp forms in fundamental domains while accounting for cusp transformations and to prove non-existence results (e.g., no non-zero weight-2 level-2 Γ0(2) cusp forms).
